admission.justification: The worklist and pure stored-item rule must preserve the same supersession semantics; otherwise an already adopted alternative reopens a closed developer decision and blocks unrelated leaf publication.

applicability: Reconsideration of base decisions in a converted leaf and the pure satisfying function applied with that evaluation's supplied superseded-decision set.
conditions: Supersession is derived from decision records of both the base and candidate; reconsider_on evaluation itself ranges only over base decisions.
The fresh worklist skips each superseded base decision before constructing items; a supplied superseded set closes a stored item with a matching parsed decision ID.
Gate and direct judging use the worklist computed for their exact current evaluation; the registered two-argument predicate retains its empty default.
exclusions: A new candidate decision raises no reconsideration item merely by being new.
An unrelated candidate decision or an omitted superseded context does not suppress an unsuperseded item.
No new trigger, transitive reconsideration, evaluation of reconsider_when prose, or changed still_rejected/raise meaning.
No promise to close a manually constructed historical item through the unchanged two-argument registered predicate.

evidence: notes/reports/reviewer/d2a83c4f-1c11-5b23-8b93-8ae61419c671/round2-record-correction/verdict.md; journal #l148-r002-c01-reviewer-record; unchanged A002 plus L148-A002-correction-01; all CODE findings closed.

statement: A decision superseded in the same leaf raises no reconsideration item.
